content:
incident-bot: ALERT: canary rollout fastpath-v3 (wave 7) in us-east-1 -> error-rate 5xx spike. Abort criteria met: 5m error_rate=3.4% (>2%), p95 latency=620ms. Pager triggered.

deploy-bot: Deploy wave id=wf-2026-03-15-07, target group=fastpath, region=us-east-1. Canary traffic=2%. Logs show upstream 502/503.

alex-k: seeing the same in Kibana - lots of 502s from model-proxy pods. sample: `"upstream_status": 502, "trace_id": "abc123"`

priya-s: Marking as rollout abort candidate. Any sign it's infra (node OOM) or app-level?

jamie-m: no OOMs on GPU nodes. CPU/ram fine. Kernel logs clean. Looks like a tenant request pattern that spikes queue processing and PROXY returns 502 when backend pool saturates.

alex-k: Can we flip the feature flag to stop routing traffic to fastpath-v3? Kill-switch exists: `flag:fastpath_v3_enabled`

priya-s: agreed. I'll flip now.

jamie-m: running ->

```
# curl to feature flag service
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://flags.redwood.internal/flags/fastpath_v3_enabled -d '{"value":false}'
{"status":"ok","flag":"fastpath_v3_enabled","value":false}
```

jamie-m: :white_check_mark: flag flipped. Routing should fall back to stable variant within seconds.

chen-l: noticed traffic drop to canary pods now. 5xx rate trending down. p95 latency back to ~220ms.

incident-bot: EVENT: abort flag toggled by jamie-m. Canary wave wf-2026-03-15-07 moved to aborted state.

priya-s: Good short-term. We should rollback the canary build and stop further waves. Alex, can you issue rollback and disable auto-rollout?

alex-k: doing rollback ->

```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/fastpath --to-revision=42
# confirmed: revision 42 (stable)
```

alex-k: auto-rollout disabled (`rollout.strategy=manual`).

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. New pods are stable. healthcheck success: 10/10 checks passing.

jamie-m: Prometheus alert for ALP-caniary-5xx cleared. Grafana dashboard shows the spike window 07:15-07:19 UTC.

priya-s: Customer impact assessment: approx 2% of traffic in us-east experienced errors for ~4 minutes. Internal tracing shows ~120 requests failed with 5xx across a handful of tenants. No SLO breaches for overall service, but SLO for fastpath slightly affected for those minutes.

alex-k: Opening incident ticket: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-0315-17 (P2). I'll attach logs and top failing trace ids.

priya-s: Postmortem checklist: 1) analyze root cause (backend proxy saturation) 2) add more robust backpressure / graceful rejection 3) adjust abort thresholds? 4) test feature flag rollback path in staging with traffic replay.

jamie-m: Quick mitigation idea: add short-lived queue depth circuit in front of model-proxy to avoid hard 502s. Will prototype.

chen-l: For handoff: I'm oncall for next shift. Taking ownership of follow-up. 

oncall-night: taking handoff - I'm up to monitor for next 6h. Please document any follow-ups in INC ticket and assign to eng-runtime for deeper fix.

priya-s: Thanks all. No further immediate actions. Leaving incident in monitoring mode. :eyes:

alex-k: thumbs-up. Closing this slack thread once handoff confirms monitoring stable. :thumbsup:
